Zoho Books credit note: should you refund the customer or apply it to an invoice? This step-by-step video shows how to create a credit note (from an invoice or from Sales > Credit Notes), how to apply it to invoices from the credit note page or the invoice page, how to refund it, how to undo an applied credit, and the 5 mistakes to avoid. beats.label: ways to use a credit note

lines: You created a credit note in Zoho Books. Now the money question: do you refund the customer, or apply it to an invoice?
Zoho Books gives you both options, and mixing them up is the easiest mistake to make.
In this video I will show you the exact clicks for both, with a simple example, and the five mistakes to avoid.
And mistake number four is the one where most people cannot find the undo button. Stay for that one.
Everything here comes from three official Zoho help pages, which I checked on the twenty sixth of November, twenty twenty six.
Zoho does not give money amounts, so every number I use is a round example, just to make it easy to follow.
And this video is about the credit note steps only, not tax treatment. Check your own tax rules separately.
First, the big question. Refund or apply?
A credit note is money you owe a customer, for example after a return.
With Apply to Invoice, you use that credit against invoices the customer has not paid yet.
With Refund, you pay the money back, and you choose the cash or bank account it comes from.
You can also split it: apply part of the credit, and keep the rest open for later.
Here is the example we will use. An invoice for one thousand dirhams, and the customer returns goods worth three hundred.
What you do next depends on one thing: has the customer already paid that invoice, or not?
Keep that question in your head. It decides everything.
So the flow looks like this.
First, you always create the credit note.
If the invoice is unpaid, the invoice itself gets credited, and I will show you how.
If the invoice is already paid, you refund the customer from the credit note. Let us build it.
Mistake number one. Starting the credit note from scratch.
If the return belongs to an invoice, do not make a blank credit note. Start from the invoice itself.
Zoho opens the New Credit Note page with the invoice details already filled in.
For returned goods, enter the exact quantity that came back under Item Details.
Zoho says the stock goes back to your inventory, and if the invoice was unpaid, it becomes Paid or Partially Paid, depending on the value returned.
And the credit note status becomes Closed, because the credit was used up.
In Zoho Books, go to Sales, then Invoices, and open the invoice the customer returned goods from.
Careful, the New button here makes a new invoice. For the credit note, you stay inside the existing invoice.
Inside the invoice, click the More icon.
Choose Create Credit Note.
The new credit note opens with the invoice details filled in.
Review the items, then save it.
No invoice to start from? Go to Sales, Credit Notes, and click New at the top right. This is the form.
Pick the customer. The Credit Note number comes from your default series, or you can set it manually with the gear icon.
Add your items, then Save as Draft if you are not ready.
Or Save as Open when you are. Open means the credit is available to use.
So mistake one is making a stand alone credit note when the return belongs to an invoice.
Start from the invoice, and the details and the stock movement are handled for you.
Mistake number two. Using the wrong path for a paid invoice.
In our example, say the customer had not paid the one thousand dirham invoice.
You create the credit note from the invoice, with a returned value of three hundred.
Zoho says the invoice becomes Paid or Partially Paid, depending on the value returned, and the credit note becomes Closed.
Now say the customer already paid the full invoice.
You still create the credit note first, the same way.
But now the three hundred is real money owed back, so the next step is a refund.
Here is the refund path.
Go to Sales, Credit Notes, and select the note.
Click More, then Refund.
Enter the refund amount, and select the cash or bank account you are refunding from.
Click Save.
You can refund the full amount or only part of it. In our example, that is three hundred, or maybe one hundred.
Zoho does not spell out here what happens to the rest, so check the credit note status on your own screen after saving.

items.text: Unpaid invoice: credit it. Paid invoice: refund it.

lines: So mistake two is trying to refund when the invoice was never paid, or forgetting to refund when it was.
Ask the paid or unpaid question first, then pick the path.
Mistakes three and four. Applying credits the right way.
Sometimes the customer does not want money back. They want the credit used on their next invoice.
That is the Apply to Invoice path, and there are two ways to start it.
Way one is from the credit note.
Go to Sales, Credit Notes, and select the note.
Click Apply to Invoice at the top.
A popup opens. Enter the amount under Credits to Apply for each invoice.
Click Save.
Way two is from the invoice. Go to Sales, Invoices, and select the invoice the customer still owes.
On that invoice page, look for Credits Available, and click the arrow next to it.
So from the invoice, click the arrow next to Credits Available.
Enter the amount under Credits to Apply.
Then click Apply Credits.

items.text: Credits Available shows only with an outstanding invoice and an open credit note

lines: Mistake number three. Looking for Credits Available and not finding it.
Zoho says it only shows when the customer has an outstanding invoice and an open credit note.
So check two things: is the invoice still unpaid, and is the credit note Open, not Draft?
Here is a quick example. A customer has an open credit of four hundred dirhams, and two unpaid invoices.
Apply two hundred and fifty to the first invoice, and one hundred and fifty to the second.
All four hundred is used, so the note becomes Closed.
If anything had been left over, the note would stay Open.
Mistake number four. Every invoice has one customer, shown here in Customer Name.
Zoho only lets you apply a credit note to invoices of that same customer, so a note for one customer cannot pay another customer's invoice.
If an invoice is missing from the Apply to Invoice popup, check the customer name first.
It is the most likely reason.
Mistake number five. Not knowing how to undo it.
Now the promise from the start. How do you undo an applied credit?
Open the credit note and go to the Credit Applied Invoices tab.
Hover over the invoice, and click the Remove icon.
The amount becomes available on the credit note again, so you can apply it somewhere else, or refund it.
Refunds have their own history. Open the credit note, and click the Refund History tab, top right.
From there, an edit icon lets you change a refund.
And a delete icon removes it.
If you have many refunds to record, there is also Import Refunds, under the More icon on the Credit Notes page.
It accepts C S V, T S V or X L S files, and Zoho gives sample files to download.
One last thing. Credit notes are for your customers. For the purchase side, Zoho Books has its own section called Vendor Credits.
I will cover that in a separate video if you want it. Tell me in the comments.
Time to put it together.

visual.title: Credit note checklist
items: Start from the invoice if you can

lines: Here is your checklist.
First, ask: is the invoice paid or unpaid?
Start the credit note from the invoice whenever the return belongs to one.
If it is unpaid, credit the invoice. If it is paid, use More, then Refund.
Credit and invoice must be the same customer, and the note must be Open.
And if you make a mistake, remove the applied credit and do it again.
That is Zoho Books credit notes, refund versus apply to invoice, with no guessing.
